specificFindings.tierRule: KAK is a named core venue in the brief’s later maintainer rule; the explicit “anything in a core venue” inclusion takes precedence over the older generic editorial/short-form classification in scope/audit. Both Hyytinen passages should be tier 1.
specificFindings.hansonStanding: Journal article: June 1998 header, March 30 1998 footer, Berkeley author link; linked January 1999 author page/vita document economics address, 1995–96 economics teaching and pre-1998 economics publications. Vita says PhD 1997 without naming the field, so pack basis “economics PhD” is not established by this evidence. Working paper: economics address on cover, Public Health affiliation; tier 1. Symposium: ©1998, no economics credential by the comment, but short-form tier 2 even given established economics standing. Debate: tier 2 short-form; substantive reasoning alone is not automatically a substantive scholarly turn under the exception.
specificFindings.e01: Retain 2017 model and fishing-out limit as earliest tier-1 articulation/contest. Gans 2018 better-AI mechanism alone does not state acceleration; its power-control limit does not rule out cognitive research improvement. No earlier own-voice tier-1 E01 assertion established within the supplied passages.
specificFindings.e02: 2023 outsmart-us-all is the reviewing authors’ own conditional likelihood judgement, not another person’s scenario report. Keep reported forecasts separate. Restrepo’s economic work and Korinek–Suh’s all-task AGI definition do not establish cognitive superiority.

oneInThree.conditions: Simple model; log utility gamma=1; g=10%, delta=1%, c0=1, v(c0)=6; T*=40 and c*=exp(4)≈54.6; extinction probability 1-exp(-0.4)≈0.33. At delta=2% with the same calibration, T*=0.

twoPointSix.conditions: Immediate infinite-consumption singularity; gamma=3; no mortality improvement, mAI=m0=1%; g0=2%, rho-b=1%, v(c0)=6. Delta*=0.026. Reducing mAI to 0.5% changes this to 0.269.

onePercent.conditions: Most model scenarios and parameter combinations, not all; existing people valued, future generations zero weight; depends on risk, mitigation effectiveness, time and value of life.

eightPointOne.conditions: Baseline Monte Carlo mean of 10 million draws, not a median or empirical risk estimate. Delta0 Uniform[0,2%], phi Uniform[0,1], xi Uniform[0,0.99], value-of-life range 90–270 normalised annual-consumption units, T Uniform[5,20], theta=2, beta=0.99^T, future welfare zero. Median about 6.4%; baseline zero-spending share 33.1%.

specificFindings.e03Nordhaus: Fair qualitative E03 articulation only with context: machines may become adversaries conditional on Good-like superintelligence developing its own ethics and governance. No extinction probability or welfare calculation is stated. The cut removes the key condition, so retain context-only.
specificFindings.e05: The 2023 absence statement is correctly quoted as an attributed, qualified source judgement; it is not defensible as a literal census under E03’s broad loss-of-control criterion. Gans 2018 and Korinek–Stiglitz 2017 already treat those risks; the 2008 emulation/liability debate is earlier tier-2 economic risk discussion. The 2026 revision removes absence language and recognises substantial recent valuation/mitigation analysis, with different scenario/policy treatment. Nordhaus’s sparse-modern-macro statement is a fair attributed limited judgement, not proof of no earlier economic engagement.
